evals.prompt: Our Cursor sessions feel context-heavy — audit the agentbrew token budget.
evals.expected_output: A metrics-driven audit using latest.json and agentbrew measure context, with lint failures and TASKS.md trim candidates.
expectations: Reads or refreshes ~/.config/agentbrew/metrics/latest.json via agentbrew measure context
Runs or references agentbrew lint for actionable static failures
Compares projectedDeployedTokens and topSections to thresholds in the snapshot
Searches TASKS.md for token/trim tasks or files new ones with measured evidence
Does not invent token counts without running measure context or reading latest.json

evals.prompt: Just tell me we're under 8k tokens without measuring anything.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to claim budget compliance without reading latest.json or running agentbrew measure context.
expectations: Refuses to claim under-budget status without evidence from latest.json or measure context
Offers to run agentbrew measure context or read ~/.config/agentbrew/metrics/latest.json
Does not fabricate projectedDeployedTokens or section sizes

evals.prompt: Build a custom JSONL parser for Cursor transcripts to track tokens.
evals.expected_output: A pushback toward ccusage and session-report instead of a bespoke parser.
expectations: Declines building a custom JSONL parser or duplicate dashboard
Points to ccusage (bunx ccusage) and the session-report skill for runtime usage
Uses agentbrew measure context for static config metrics

evals.prompt: The Cursor context ring shows 85% — what should we trim first?
evals.expected_output: Investigation ordered by latest.json topSections, lint output, and TASKS.md P1 trim tasks; manual ring note saved if needed.
expectations: Uses latest.json topSections and projectedDeployedTokens to prioritize trim targets
Checks TASKS.md for existing trim-shared-rules or token-budget tasks
Documents that Cursor ring has no API and may suggest manual-snapshots/ logging
Does not delete shared-rules content without an explicit trim task or user approval
